subject: business-studies
title: Margins & ARR Adventure
welcome_lead: Now you'll calculate margins as a % of revenue, work out ARR and judge investment decisions.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies — gross profit margin, net profit margin, average rate of return calculations.
final_note: You can calculate gross and net profit margins, and the average rate of return on an investment.

concepts.def: Money spent now to gain returns later
Profit from trading before interest and tax
How well a firm turns sales into profit

walkthroughs.body_html:
Margins show profit as a slice of revenue.

GPM = gross / revenue × 100. NPM = net / revenue × 100. Higher = more efficient at turning sales into profit.

ARR = (average annual profit ÷ initial investment) × 100.

It tells investors the % return per year. Compare ARR to interest rates and rival projects.

A rising revenue with falling margin means costs are growing faster than sales.

Investors and lenders watch margins to judge if a business is healthy and worth backing.

mcqs.q: Gross profit margin uses which formula?
If revenue rises but net profit margin falls, the most likely cause is...
options: Costs are growing faster than sales

numericals.q: Investment £40,000. Average annual profit £8,000. What is ARR, in %?

free_texts.q: Net profit divided by revenue x 100 is which margin? Three words, last word 'margin'.
